headline: Data Centers Pay Own Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill, reinforced by recent regulatory decisions, shifts the financial burden of dedicated grid infrastructure for large energy users like data centers directly to those companies, aiming to decrease residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, environmental groups
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Centers to Pay for Own Power Lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission has ruled that data centers must bear the full cost of transmission infrastructure projects they require, preventing these billions of dollars in costs from falling on residential ratepayers. Governor Abigail Spanberger praised the decision, stating it will save Virginians hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Centers Report Water Usage
short_summary: This legislation mandates that data centers in Virginia report their water consumption to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact on water resources.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Be Made Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, which will be publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about the industry's significant water consumption and its impact on dwindling groundwater supplies.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill empowers localities to impose noise limits and siting requirements on data centers, addressing community concerns about noise pollution and the impact of large-scale development.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data center sites, environmental groups
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry
news_headline: Data Centers May Need Noise, Energy Disclosure Under New Rules
news_summary: Under HB153/SB94, facilities requiring 100 megawatts or more, likely data centers, would trigger special-exception submission requirements, including a noise study for nearby residences and schools. Fairfax County staff proposes these requirements, along with an energy-provider statement on anticipated demand and source.
